title: Getting Started with Color Themes
text: "colortheme" object provides two color-generating functions: palette() ramp(). palette() function accepts integer nn returns vector nn discrete colors. primarily intended qualitative themes, distinct colors used represent categorical data. ramp() function accepts numeric vector xx values [0,1][0, 1] interval returns vector corresponding colors. maps numeric values onto continuous color gradient (stepped color bands), making suitable sequential diverging themes well binned scales.

title: Getting Started with Color Themes
text: can get pre-defined "colortheme" object providing theme name colortheme() function.  palette ramp functions accessible via $ operator.  palette ramp can also extracted using corresponding helper functions; as_palette() as_ramp(). can modify themes reversing color order changing theme type (e.g., sequential qualitative). Note converting theme @qualitative also turns $ramp() stepped (binned) color ramp default. changes can applied two ways: Using Arguments : provide appropriate argument function, reverse = TRUE type = "qualitative". Using Suffixes : convenience, can append suffix directly theme’s name. _r reverse theme, @q (longer, @qual) make theme qualitative (@d diverging, @s sequential).   can also customize kernel arguments option parameters fly using query parameters ? (e.g., "highlight?=1:2" "viridis?ramp.steps=5").   setting ramp.steps (either integer equal bins numeric vector cutoffs (0,1)(0, 1)), continuous theme can quantized stepped color ramp:   multiple packages provide theme name (e.g., "Paired"), can specify one use two ways: Using Argument : provide package name source argument (e.g., source = "grDevices"). Using Prefix : prepend package name forward slash theme name (e.g., "RColorBrewer/Paired").
code: library(colortheme) # diverging color theme "azurerose" (package:colortheme) azurerose <- colortheme("azurerose") print(azurerose) #> Diverging Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #005AAD, #3B78C2, #729BD6, #AFC4E8, #F7F7F7, #E8B3CC, #D67FA8, #BD4989, #A4136E #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 9L #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "ramp" #>   alpha: NA azurerose$palette(5) #> [1] "#005AAD" "#729BD6" "#F7F7F7" "#D67FA8" "#A4136E" azurerose$ramp(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1)) #>  [1] "#005AAD" "#3372BE" "#5E8DCE" "#8BABDD" "#BECEEB" "#F7F7F7" "#ECC1D4" #>  [8] "#DE94B6" "#CC6A9B" "#B84084" "#A4136E" # sequential color theme "viridis" (package:viridisLite) viridis <- colortheme("viridis") print(viridis) #> Sequential Color Theme: 'viridis' (from 'viridisLite') #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Kernel Function: #> function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D") #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : Inf #>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$direction <- - kernel.args$direction" #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   option   : "viridis" #>   alpha    : 1 #>   begin    : 0.2 #>   end      : 0.8 #>   direction: 1 as_palette(viridis)(5) #> [1] "#414487FF" "#2F6C8EFF" "#21908CFF" "#2FB47CFF" "#7AD151FF" as_ramp(viridis)(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1)) #>  [1] "#414487" "#3A548C" "#32658E" "#2C738E" "#26828E" "#21918C" "#1F9F88" #>  [8] "#26AD81" "#3ABA76" "#58C666" "#7AD151" colortheme("azurerose", reverse = TRUE, type = "q") #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #A4136E, #BD4989, #D67FA8, #E8B3CC, #F7F7F7, #AFC4E8, #729BD6, #3B78C2, #005AAD #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 9L #>   palette.formatter: "recycle" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "palette" #>   alpha: NA colortheme("azurerose_r@qualitative") #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #A4136E, #BD4989, #D67FA8, #E8B3CC, #F7F7F7, #AFC4E8, #729BD6, #3B78C2, #005AAD #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 9L #>   palette.formatter: "recycle" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "palette" #>   alpha: NA colortheme("viridis", type = "q", kernel.size = 7, begin = 0, end = 1) #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'viridis' (from 'viridisLite') #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Kernel Function: #> function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D") #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 7 #>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$direction <- - kernel.args$direction" #>   palette.formatter: "recycle" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   option   : "viridis" #>   alpha    : 1 #>   begin    : 0 #>   end      : 1 #>   direction: 1 colortheme("viridis@qual?kernel.size=7;begin=0;end=1") #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'viridis' (from 'viridisLite') #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Kernel Function: #> function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D") #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 7 #>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$direction <- - kernel.args$direction" #>   palette.formatter: "recycle" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   option   : "viridis" #>   alpha    : 1 #>   begin    : 0 #>   end      : 1 #>   direction: 1 # Quantize into 5 equal steps colortheme("azurerose?ramp.steps=5") #> Diverging Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #005AAD, #3B78C2, #729BD6, #AFC4E8, #F7F7F7, #E8B3CC, #D67FA8, #BD4989, #A4136E #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 9L #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : 5 #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "ramp" #>   alpha: NA # Split at custom cutoffs to create a desired ramp colortheme("azurerose?ramp.steps=seq.int(.4, .6, by=.02)") #> Diverging Color Theme: 'azurerose' (from 'colortheme') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #005AAD, #3B78C2, #729BD6, #AFC4E8, #F7F7F7, #E8B3CC, #D67FA8, #BD4989, #A4136E #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 9L #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : c(0.4, 0.42, 0.44, 0.46, 0.48, 0.5, 0.52, 0.54, 0.56, 0.58, 0.6) #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "ramp" #>   alpha: NA # qualitative color theme "Paired" (package:grDevices) colortheme("Paired", source = "grDevices") #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'Paired' (from 'grDevices') #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Kernel Function: #> function (n = NULL, palette = "Okabe-Ito", alpha, recycle = FALSE, names = FALSE) #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 12L #>   palette.formatter: "recycle" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : 12 #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   palette: "Paired" #>   alpha  : NULL #>   recycle: FALSE # qualitative color theme "Paired" (package:RColorBrewer) colortheme("RColorBrewer/Paired") #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'Paired' (from 'RColorBrewer') #>  #> title: Getting Started with Color Themes
text: Alternatively, can create new "colortheme" object passing custom color vector function first argument colortheme().   can register custom theme call name later current R session. , use register_colortheme() function.
code: # create a new color theme using a color vector mytheme <- colortheme(   c("#003f5c", "#7a5195", "#ef5675", "#ffa600"),   type = "sequential", name = "mytheme" ) print(mytheme) #> Sequential Color Theme: 'mytheme' #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #003f5c, #7a5195, #ef5675, #ffa600 #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 4L #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "ramp" #>   alpha: NA as_palette(mytheme)(5) #> [1] "#003F5C" "#624E86" "#B85585" "#F46C63" "#FFA600" as_ramp(mytheme)(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1)) #>  [1] "#003F5C" "#33466D" "#534B7E" "#70508F" "#94538F" "#B85585" "#D9567C" #>  [8] "#F15F6E" "#F77958" "#FC903C" "#FFA600" # create a new color theme using a color function rainbow <- colortheme(   grDevices::rainbow,   name = "rainbow", source = "grDevices" ) print(rainbow) #> Sequential Color Theme: 'rainbow' (from 'grDevices') #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Kernel Function: #> function (n, s = 1, v = 1, start = 0, end = max(1, n - 1)/n, alpha, rev = FALSE) #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : Inf #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA as_palette(rainbow)(5) #> [1] "#FF0000" "#CCFF00" "#00FF66" "#0066FF" "#CC00FF" as_ramp(rainbow)(seq.int(0, 1, by = 0.1)) #>  [1] "#FF0000" "#FF9800" "#CDFF00" "#35FF00" "#00FF64" "#00FFFC" "#006AFF" #>  [8] "#2F00FF" "#C700FF" "#FF009E" "#FF0006" register_colortheme(mytheme, name = "mytheme", source = "custom") colortheme("custom/mytheme@q") #> Qualitative Color Theme: 'mytheme' (from 'custom') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #003f5c, #7a5195, #ef5675, #ffa600 #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 4L #>   palette.formatter: "recycle" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "palette" #>   alpha: NA colortheme("mytheme_r@div?alpha=.5") #> Diverging Color Theme: 'mytheme' (from 'custom') #>  #> Kernel Class: color #>  #> Kernel Colors: #> #ffa600, #ef5675, #7a5195, #003f5c #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : 4L #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>   reverse.method   : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   mode : "ramp" #>   alpha: 0.5

title: Getting Started with Color Themes
text: apply color themes ggplot2 plots, use scale_color_theme() scale_fill_theme() functions. scales integrate themes directly plot’s color fill aesthetics.
code: library(ggplot2) theme_set(theme_minimal())  set.seed(42) dataset <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 5000L), ]  p <- ggplot(dataset) + geom_point(aes(carat, price, col = color)) p + scale_color_theme("shiki") p + scale_color_theme("viridisLite/mako", discrete = TRUE) p + scale_color_theme("tokyo@qual") p + scale_color_theme("highlight?which=list(1, 6:7);base='transparent'") p2 <- ggplot(dataset) +   geom_histogram(aes(x = carat, fill = cut), bins = 20) p2 + scale_fill_theme("ukiyoe") p2 + scale_fill_theme("highlight_r?which=list(1:2, 5)") p2 + scale_fill_theme("ai@q") p2 + scale_fill_theme("Zissou 1_r@q") # Continuous and stepped scales with sequential, diverging, and qualitative themes p3 <- ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_raster() + theme(legend.position = "right") p3 + scale_fill_theme("ai") p3 + scale_fill_theme("Cividis", middle = 0.02) p3 + scale_fill_theme("steps", middle = 0.02) p3 + scale_fill_theme("magma?ramp.steps=6&alpha=0.8")

what: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: colortheme lightweight R package providing unified interface managing, customizing, applying qualitative, sequential, diverging color themes. acts versatile bridge base R graphics, custom color definitions, popular palette collections (grDevices, viridisLite, RColorBrewer, khroma, etc.), offering seamless scale integration ggplot2.

title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: Unified Dispatcher (colortheme()): Effortlessly retrieve registered themes name, build themes color vectors functions, modify existing themes fly. Compact Query Syntax: Customize themes instantly using query strings (e.g., reversing order _r, specifying types @qual, discretizing gradients ?ramp.steps=5, adjusting transparency ?alpha=0.5;na.color='gray'). Dual Functional Interface: Extract discrete palette functions ($palette(n)) continuous/stepped color ramp functions ($ramp(x)) theme. Base R Data Mapping (map_to_colors()): Directly map discrete continuous vectors hexadecimal color codes base R plots. Seamless ggplot2 Scales: Automatically apply discrete continuous scales using scale_color_theme() scale_fill_theme(), complete proper midpoint handling diverging palettes.

title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps

code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("ryo-asashi/colortheme")

title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: colorthemes() helps find color theme. can filter registry name, source, type using case-insensitive prefix matching. find theme, colortheme() serves central interface load use . can retrieve pre-defined palettes apply compact query syntax reverse colors, change types, inject options.
code: library(colortheme)  # Find color themes matching "ma" colorthemes("ma") #>      name      source       type #> 1 managua      khroma  diverging #> 2 Magenta   grDevices sequential #> 3   magma viridisLite sequential #> 4    mako viridisLite sequential #> 5    Mako   grDevices sequential  # Find qualitative color themes from a specific source colorthemes(source = "RColorBrewer", type = "qualitative") #>      name       source        type #> 1  Accent RColorBrewer qualitative #> 2   Dark2 RColorBrewer qualitative #> 3  Paired RColorBrewer qualitative #> 4 Pastel1 RColorBrewer qualitative #> 5 Pastel2 RColorBrewer qualitative #> 6    Set1 RColorBrewer qualitative #> 7    Set2 RColorBrewer qualitative #> 8    Set3 RColorBrewer qualitative # Retrieve a built-in sequential theme and generate colors ct <- colortheme("Viridis") ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#4B0055" "#00588B" "#009B95" "#53CC67" "#FDE333" ct$ramp(seq.int(0, 1, length.out = 5)) #> [1] "#4B0055" "#00588B" "#009B95" "#53CC67" "#FDE333"  # Use query syntax for on-the-fly modifications ct_custom <- colortheme("grDevices/Zissou 1_r@qual?alpha=0.75") ct_custom$palette(4L) #> [1] "#F5191CBF" "#E8A419BF" "#9FC095BF" "#3B99B1BF"

title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: Using as_palette() as_ramp(), can easily extract clean color-generating functions custom graphics workflows.
code: # Extract a discrete palette function taking n pal <- as_palette("Okabe-Ito") pal(6L) #> [1] "#000000" "#E69F00" "#56B4E9" "#009E73" "#F0E442" "#0072B2"  # Extract a continuous ramp function taking x in [0, 1] ramp <- as_ramp("bluescale") ramp(c(0, 0.5, 1.0)) #> [1] "#132B43" "#336A98" "#56B1F7"

what: 3. Direct Mapping for Base R Graphics (map_to_colors())
title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: map_to_colors() automatically handles factor/character variables (qualitative) numeric vectors (sequential/diverging) proper scaling NA management.
code: # Continuous mapping (Sequential & Step-wise sequential) par(mfrow = c(1L, 2L), mar = c(3, 3, 1, 1)) plot(cars, col = map_to_colors(cars$speed), pch = 19, cex = 1.2) plot(cars, col = map_to_colors(cars$speed, "ukiyoe@seq"), pch = 19, cex = 1.2) # Discrete mapping (Qualitative) plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width,      col = map_to_colors(iris$Species), pch = 19, cex = 1.2) plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width,      col = map_to_colors(iris$Species, "muted"), pch = 19, cex = 1.2)

title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: scale_color_theme() automatically detects whether theme qualitative continuous, configuring appropriate ggplot2 scales hood. Diverging themes automatically leverage scales::rescale_mid() midpoint specified.
code: library(ggplot2)  # Qualitative scale ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) +   geom_point(size = 3) +   scale_color_theme("Set2") # Continuous diverging scale with custom midpoint ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_tile() +   scale_fill_theme("Cividis", middle = 0.02)

title: A Unified Framework and Interface for Color Palettes and Ramps
text: can emphasize specific categories quantize continuous gradients discrete intervals directly query string—without modifying data switching scale functions. Discrete Highlighting ("highlight"): Emphasizes target categories specified using accent colors keeping others base gray. Supports negative indices (e.g., -1 last category) list() inputs group multiple categories accent color.   Stepped / Binned Ramps (?ramp.steps=...): theme can converted stepped ramp setting ramp.steps integer kk (kk equal bins) numeric vector cutoffs (0,1)(0, 1).
code: # Discrete highlighting (emphasize the 1st category) ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) +   geom_point(size = 3) +   scale_color_theme("highlight") # Discrete highlighting (emphasize the 2nd category and the 3rd category) ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) +   geom_point(size = 3) +   scale_color_theme("highlight_r?which=list(2L, -1L)") # Step-wise diverging scale (quantize 'Temps' into 12 discrete bands) ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_tile() +   scale_fill_theme("Temps?ramp.steps=12L", middle = 0.02) # Step-wise qualitative scale (use 'ukiyoe' colors as discrete bands) ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_tile() +   scale_fill_theme("ukiyoe@s")

text: colortheme() returns "colortheme" object (environment class c("colortheme", "environment")) containing $palette() $ramp() functions along theme metadata.

title: Color Themes for Graphics — colortheme
text: "colortheme" object specialized environment provides two primary color-generating functions: $palette() $ramp(). $palette(n) takes integer n returns character vector n discrete colors. primarily intended qualitative themes, distinct colors represent categorical data. $ramp(x) takes numeric vector x values [0, 1] interval returns character vector corresponding colors. maps numeric values onto continuous color gradient, making suitable sequential diverging themes. colortheme() dispatches based class object: object character string (e.g., "Viridis", "grDevices/RdBu_r@q?alpha=.5"), parsed according theme name syntax loaded registry. object color kernel (character vector colors, palette function, ramp function), new color theme constructed. object already "colortheme" object, modified copy returned updated settings.

title: Color Themes for Graphics — colortheme
text: retrieving registered theme string, can use compact URL-like syntax specify source apply --fly modifications: "[(source)/](name)[_r][@(type)][?(query)]" source: (optional) source package collection (e.g., "grDevices"). name: name theme (e.g., "RdBu"). "_r": (optional) suffix reverse color order. type: (optional) desired theme type, matched "sequential", "diverging", "qualitative" (abbreviations like "s", "d", "q" "seq", "div", "qual" supported). query: (optional) key-value pairs separated ; & (e.g., "?alpha=0.5;na.color='gray50'") override theme metadata, options, kernel.args.

title: Color Themes for Graphics — colortheme
code: # Retrieve a pre-defined theme ct <- colortheme("Mako") print(ct) #> Sequential Color Theme: 'Mako' (from 'grDevices') #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Kernel Function: #> function (n, palette = "viridis", alpha = NULL, rev = FALSE, fixup = TRUE) #>  #> Options: #>   kernel.size      : Inf #>   reverse.method   : "kernel.args$rev <- !kernel.args$rev" #>   palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>   palette.reverse  : FALSE #>   ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>   ramp.steps       : Inf #>   na.color         : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>   palette: "Mako" #>   alpha  : NULL #>   rev    : FALSE #>   ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#070707" "#423460" "#007FA8" "#48C2B4" "#E0F7E1" ct$ramp(seq.int(0, 1, length.out = 5)) #> [1] "#070707" "#423560" "#0080A8" "#48C2B4" "#E0F7E1"  # Use special syntax to get a reversed, qualitative theme with alpha ct <- colortheme("grDevices/Zissou 1_r@qual?alpha=0.75") ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#F5191CBF" "#E78F0ABF" "#EACB2BBF" "#7CBA96BF" "#3B99B1BF"  # Create a new theme from a vector of colors ct <- colortheme(c("#003f5c", "#7a5195", "#ef5675", "#ffa600")) ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#003F5C" "#624E86" "#B85585" "#F46C63" "#FFA600"  # Modify an existing theme ct2 <- colortheme(ct, type = "qualitative", reverse = TRUE) ct2$palette(5L) #> [1] "#ffa600" "#ef5675" "#7a5195" "#003f5c" "#ffa600"

what: List, Register, and Configure Color Themes — colorthemes
title: List, Register, and Configure Color Themes — colorthemes
text: colorthemes() returns data frame listing available color themes registry. register_colortheme() registers custom color theme registry. colortheme_options() sets retrieves global package options.

code: colorthemes(name = NULL, source = NULL, type = NULL, env = NULL)  register_colortheme(   kernel,   kernel.args = list(),   options = list(),   name = "newtheme",   source = "custom",   type = NULL,   env = NULL )  colortheme_options(...)

title: List, Register, and Configure Color Themes — colorthemes
text: name colorthemes(), character vector theme names match (case-insensitive prefix matching). register_colortheme(), single string new theme name. source colorthemes(), character vector sources match (case-insensitive prefix matching). register_colortheme(), single string source name. type character string vector specifying theme type(s): "sequential", "diverging", "qualitative". env environment color themes registered. Defaults package registry (getOption("colortheme.registry")). kernel color vector, palette function, ramp function, "colortheme" object, length-2 character vector/list lazy evaluation. NULL, theme removed. kernel.args list arguments passed color kernel. options list option values controlling color theme's behavior. ... colortheme_options(), options defined name = value form, single named list options, character strings specifying option names retrieve.

title: List, Register, and Configure Color Themes — colorthemes
text: colorthemes(): data frame columns "name", "source", "type". register_colortheme(): Invisibly returns metadata previous theme overwritten (NULL none existed). colortheme_options(): named list current option values (called arguments character strings), invisibly named list previous values (setting options).

title: List, Register, and Configure Color Themes — colorthemes
text: colorthemes() extracts metadata registry environment structures data frame, allowing users discover themes name, source, type (case-insensitive prefix matching). register_colortheme() takes color vector, color-generating function, existing "colortheme" object registers specified name source (defaulting "custom/newtheme"). keep registry lightweight, kernel argument supports lazy loading: pass character vector list length 2 first element R expression returning kernel (e.g., "rainbow") second namespace (e.g., "grDevices"). colortheme_options() provides scoped interface R's global options(), automatically prefixing option names colortheme.. Supported options "sequential", "diverging", "qualitative" (default theme names objects), "registry" (active registry environment).

title: List, Register, and Configure Color Themes — colorthemes
code: # List all available themes head(colorthemes()) #>            name    source      type #> 1      ArmyRose grDevices diverging #> 2        Berlin grDevices diverging #> 3      Blue-Red grDevices diverging #> 4    Blue-Red 2 grDevices diverging #> 5    Blue-Red 3 grDevices diverging #> 6 Blue-Yellow 2 grDevices diverging  # Case-insensitive prefix matching colorthemes(name = "ma") #>      name      source       type #> 1 managua      khroma  diverging #> 2 Magenta   grDevices sequential #> 3    Mako   grDevices sequential #> 4   magma viridisLite sequential #> 5    mako viridisLite sequential  # Register a custom theme and remove it afterward register_colortheme(   kernel = c("#264653", "#2a9d8f", "#e9c46a", "#f4a261", "#e76f51"),   name = "sand", source = "custom", type = "sequential" ) colorthemes(name = "sand") #>   name source       type #> 1 sand custom sequential register_colortheme(NULL, name = "sand", source = "custom")  # View, modify, and restore global options colortheme_options() #> $diverging #> [1] "azurerose" #>  #> $qualitative #> [1] "hcl" #>  #> $registry #> <environment: 0x5c2a1edd2600> #>  #> $sequential #> [1] "bluescale" #>  old <- colortheme_options(sequential = "Viridis") colortheme_options("sequential") #> $sequential #> [1] "Viridis" #>  colortheme_options(old)

what: Map Values to Colors using Color Themes — map_to_colors
title: Map Values to Colors using Color Themes — map_to_colors
text: map_to_colors() maps vector data values vector hexadecimal color codes based specified color theme. automatically handles discrete continuous variables, appropriately scaling values handling missing data.

title: Map Values to Colors using Color Themes — map_to_colors
code: map_to_colors(x, theme = NULL, discrete = NULL, middle = 0, na.value = NULL)

title: Map Values to Colors using Color Themes — map_to_colors
text: x vector data values (discrete continuous) mapped colors. theme color theme name (e.g., "Viridis"), "colortheme" object, character vector color names, palette/ramp function. See colortheme details. discrete logical. TRUE, discrete scale used regardless data type theme type. middle numeric value specifying midpoint diverging color themes. Default 0. na.value character string specifying color NA values. NULL (default), falls back theme's na.color option.

title: Map Values to Colors using Color Themes — map_to_colors
text: character vector hexadecimal color codes.

title: Map Values to Colors using Color Themes — map_to_colors
code: # Continuous mapping (Sequential) plot(cars, col = map_to_colors(cars$speed, "Viridis"), pch = 19)   # Discrete mapping (Qualitative) plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width,      col = map_to_colors(iris$Species, "Set 2"), pch = 19)

title: Color Theme Scales for ggplot2 Graphics — scale_color_theme
text: function automatically selects appropriate ggplot2 scale based theme's type: theme "qualitative", discrete scale used default (discrete = TRUE). theme "sequential" "diverging", continuous scale used default. Diverging themes use scales::rescale_mid() center gradient around middle.

title: Color Theme Scales for ggplot2 Graphics — scale_color_theme
code: d <- ggplot2::ggplot(iris, ggplot2::aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) +   ggplot2::geom_point() d + scale_color_theme("Set 1")  d + scale_color_theme("SunsetDark", discrete = TRUE)
